title: Computer Vision Lab
objectives: Know that images are grids of numbers (pixels)
Tell classification, detection, and facial recognition apart
Train an image classifier the way pros do
Spot Computer Vision in the real world

stages.title: Give Computers Eyes!
stages.narration: A photo is just a giant grid of numbers to a computer. Computer Vision finds patterns in those numbers so machines can understand what they see. Let's explore how!

steps.text: The computer sees it as a grid of number-pixels.
Computer Vision hunts for patterns in those numbers.

stages.title: Spot Computer Vision
stages.prompt: Tap everything that uses Computer Vision to understand images.

feedback.correct: Yes! This 'sees' and understands images, that's Computer Vision.
feedback.incorrect: This works without looking at images, so it does not use Computer Vision.

stages.title: Classification vs Detection
stages.prompt: Image Classification gives the WHOLE picture one label. Object Detection finds and boxes EACH thing. Sort each job into the right bucket.
stages.note: Classification = one label for the whole image. Detection = find and box every object separately.

cards.label: Draw a box around every car
Mark each face in a crowd

stages.title: Name That Vision Task
stages.prompt: Three big Computer Vision jobs. Pick the right one for each task.

tasks.label: Sort photos into 'cat' or 'dog' albums
tasks.explain: One label for the whole photo, that's image classification.

tasks.label: Box every pedestrian for a self-driving car
tasks.explain: Finding and boxing each object is object detection.

tasks.label: Unlock a phone by matching its owner's face
tasks.explain: Matching a face to a specific person is facial recognition.

tasks.label: Tag a whole picture as 'sunset'
tasks.explain: The entire image gets a single label, so it's classification.

tasks.label: Outline all products on a store shelf
tasks.explain: Locating many separate items means object detection.

tasks.label: Recognize which friend is in a photo
tasks.explain: Identifying a known person by their face is facial recognition.

stages.title: Train a Gesture Classifier
stages.prompt: Just like Google Teachable Machine, feed the model labeled webcam frames. Watch the accuracy climb as it learns each gesture!

test.prompt: A brand new webcam frame arrives. What will YOUR model predict?

stages.explain: You just followed the real workflow: collect examples, train the model, test on a new image. Varied examples (angles, lighting) make it even smarter.

stages.title: Computer Vision in the Real World
stages.prompt: Tap each place to discover how Computer Vision helps there. Visit them all!

locations.label: Your Phone
locations.info: Face Unlock uses Computer Vision to recognize your face and open the phone instantly.

locations.label: Hospital
locations.info: AI reads X-rays and scans to help doctors spot illness earlier and more accurately.

locations.label: Self-Driving Car
locations.info: Cameras plus Computer Vision detect pedestrians, lanes, and stop signs to drive safely.

locations.label: Farm
locations.info: Drones with cameras check crop health and spot pests from high above the fields.

locations.label: Smart Store
locations.info: Cameras recognize products at checkout, so there's no need to scan barcodes one by one.

stages.title: Vision Final Test
stages.prompt: Score at least 80% to earn your Vision Voyager badge.

questions.q: What does Computer Vision let machines do?
questions.explain: Computer Vision helps computers 'see' and understand visual information.

questions.q: To a computer, an image is really made of...
questions.explain: Every image is stored as numbers describing each pixel's color.

questions.q: Labeling a WHOLE photo as 'cat' is called...
questions.explain: Classification gives the entire image one label.

questions.q: Finding and boxing each object in a photo is...
questions.explain: Detection locates and boxes individual objects.

questions.q: Matching a face to a specific person is...
questions.explain: Facial recognition identifies a known person by their face.

questions.q: Which of these uses Computer Vision?
questions.explain: Face Unlock 'sees' your face, that's Computer Vision. A calculator just follows rules.

questions.q: How do you make an image classifier more accurate?
questions.explain: More examples from different angles and lighting help it recognize each class.

questions.q: What are the 3 steps to build a classifier?
questions.explain: Collect examples, train the model, then test it, just like Teachable Machine.

stages.title: Lab Complete!
messages: 🏆 You earned the Vision Voyager Badge
You trained an image classifier and helped a computer see
